games.title: Tool Picker
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to select from and use a range of tools and equipment to perform practical tasks [for example, cutting, shaping, joining and finishing]
games.instruction: Think about the job, then tap the best tool.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about what the job needs the tool to do.

questions.ask: Which tool is best for cutting paper?
Which tool is best for sticking two sheets of paper together?
Which tool helps you draw a straight line?
Which tool makes a neat hole in paper?
Which tool is best for stirring a cake mix?
Which tool measures how long a strip of card is?
Which tool could join two pieces of fabric?
How should you carry scissors safely?
Which tool spreads butter on bread safely?

games.title: Material Match
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to select from and use a wide range of materials and components, including construction materials, textiles and ingredients, according to their characteristics
games.instruction: Think about what it is made of, then tap the group.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about how it feels and what it is made of.

questions.ask: Which group does a T-shirt usually belong in?
Which group does a window pane usually belong in?
Which group does a saucepan usually belong in?
Which group does a cereal box belong in?
Which group does a seaside bucket usually belong in?
Which group does a sock belong in?
Which group does a paper clip belong in?
Which group does a page in a book belong in?
Which group does a garden fence usually belong in?

games.title: Healthy Plate
games.skillName: Sorting foods for a healthy diet
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to use the basic principles of a healthy and varied diet to prepare dishes
games.instruction: Think about the food, then tap its group.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about what kind of food it is.

questions.ask: Which group does an apple belong in?
Which group does bread belong in?
Which group does cheese belong in?
Which group does fish belong in?
Which group do sweets belong in?
Which group does pasta belong in?
Which group does a carrot belong in?
Which group do eggs belong in?
Which group does yoghurt belong in?

games.title: Farm To Fork
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to understand where food comes from
games.instruction: Read the clues, then tap the food.
games.hint: Not quite. Read the clues again and picture the farm.

questions.ask: I come from cows and I am white. What am I?
Bees make me from the nectar of flowers. What am I?
Hens lay me. What am I?
I am made by grinding wheat and I am used to make bread. What am I?
I grow under the ground and can be mashed or made into chips. What am I?
I grow on trees in an orchard and can be red or green. What am I?
I am made from milk and cheddar is one kind of me. What am I?
I am an orange root that grows in the soil. What am I?
I am a fish caught at sea and often served with chips. What am I?

games.title: Who Is It For?
games.skillName: Designing for a user and purpose
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to design purposeful, functional, appealing products for themselves and other users based on design criteria
games.instruction: Think about who will use it, then tap the best answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about who will use it and what it must do.

questions.ask: Who is a rattle designed for?
A cup for a toddler should be...
Why does a raincoat need to be waterproof?
A bag for carrying books needs to be...
What is a sun hat with a wide brim for?
A lunchbox needs a lid that...
Party hats for a birthday should look...
A toy for a baby must NOT have...
A pencil pot must be able to...

games.title: Product Detectives
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to explore and evaluate a range of existing products; evaluate their ideas and products against design criteria
games.instruction: Think about what the product does, then tap the reason.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about how the product is used.

questions.ask: Why does a toothbrush have a long handle?
Why are wellies made of rubber?
Why do scissors for children have rounded tips?
Why does a mug have a handle?
Why is a bike helmet hard?
Why is a teddy bear made of soft fabric?
When you test a product, what should you ask?
Why does a lunchbox have a clip on the lid?
Why do many drink bottles have a screw lid?

games.title: Slide And Lever Lab
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to explore and use mechanisms [for example, levers, sliders, wheels and axles], in their products
games.instruction: Think about how it moves, then tap its group.
games.hint: Not quite. Does it move in a straight line, or turn on a pivot?

questions.ask: A card strip moves a rocket up and down a slot. Which group?
A card arm turns around a split pin to wave. Which group?
A drawer moves in and out in a straight line. Which group?
A seesaw tips up and down around its middle. Which group?
A toy car rolls along on round parts. Which group?
What is the point that a lever turns around called?
What can you use as a pivot in a card picture?
What is the gap cut for a slider to move along?
How does a slider move?

games.title: Wheels On The Go
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to explore and use mechanisms [for example, levers, sliders, wheels and axles], in their products
games.instruction: Think about how wheels turn, then tap the answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about how a wheel rolls on its axle.

questions.ask: What is the rod that joins two wheels called?
Which shape must a wheel be to roll smoothly?
Where should the hole for the axle go in a wheel?
How many wheels does a bicycle have?
Which of these has wheels and axles?
How many wheels does a wheelbarrow usually have?
Why might a wheel wobble as it rolls?
What could you use as a simple axle on a model?
What could hold an axle onto a model but let it turn?

games.title: Tower Test
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to build structures, exploring how they can be made stronger, stiffer and more stable
games.instruction: Read it, then decide if it is true or false.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about towers that wobble and towers that stand firm.

questions.ask: A wide base helps a tower stand up.
A tall, thin tower is more stable than a short, wide one.
Folding card makes it stiffer.
Rolling paper into a tube makes it stronger.
A flat sheet of paper is stiffer than a folded one.
Putting heavy blocks at the top makes a tower more stable.
Wet card is stronger than dry card.
A bridge is a kind of structure.
Joining card with lots of tape can make a model stronger.

games.title: Idea Builder
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to generate, develop, model and communicate their ideas through talking, drawing, templates, mock-ups and, where appropriate, information and communication technology
games.instruction: Think about how designers share ideas, then tap the answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about how you could show your idea to someone else.

questions.ask: What is a quick model of your idea made from paper or card?
What can you draw around to cut the same shape again and again?
What is a good way to show your idea before you make it?
How can you share your idea with a friend?
What should you add to your drawing to explain it?
Why make a mock-up before the real thing?
What can a computer help you do with an idea?
After talking with a friend, you might...
